keyTerms.definition: The complete correct response each key entry gives.
A wrong-answer pattern the key warns against.
Point breakdown per question.

recall.question: What does each key entry provide?
recall.answer: Strong answers, red flags, and rubrics.

keyTerms.definition: p(x) = sum_z p(z)p(x|z); integral when continuous.
p(x,z) = p(z)p(x|z): what you sum over z.

recall.question: Write p(x) for discrete and continuous z.
recall.answer: p(x) = sum_z p(z)p(x|z). Continuous: p(x) = integral p(z)p(x|z) dz.

recall.question: Q1's red flag?
recall.answer: Writing the joint as the answer.

keyTerms.definition: p(z|x): belief over hidden causes after data.
p(x|z): scores data under a fixed cause.

recall.question: Posterior vs likelihood?
recall.answer: The posterior is the belief over hidden causes after data; the likelihood scores data under a fixed cause. They point in opposite causal directions.

keyTerms.definition: E_q[log p(x|z)] - KL(q(z)||p(z)).
E_q[log p(x|z)]: rewards reconstructions of the data.

recall.question: State the ELBO and each term's role.
recall.answer: ELBO = E_q[log p(x|z)] - KL(q(z)||p(z)). The first rewards reconstructions; the second pulls q toward the prior and charges for latent information.

recall.question: Q3's red flag?
recall.answer: Calling the KL term a prior; it is a divergence, not a law.

keyTerms.definition: KL(q(z)||p(z|x)) = log p(x) - ELBO.
log p(x): the ELBO plus the gap.

recall.question: When is the gap zero?
recall.answer: Exactly when q equals the true posterior.

recall.question: Q4's red flag?
recall.answer: Claiming a large ELBO means a small gap.

keyTerms.definition: KL(q||p): mode-seeking; what VI minimizes.
Mode-covering; what maximum likelihood minimizes.

recall.question: Which KL does VI minimize, and what behavior does it imply?
recall.answer: Reverse KL, KL(q||p): mode-seeking; q sits on posterior modes and may drop minor ones.

keyTerms.definition: z = g(theta, eps) with fixed noise; fails for discrete latents.
eps ~ fixed law: what makes the sampling law independent of theta.

recall.question: What does the trick buy, and where does it fail?
recall.answer: Low-variance gradients through sampling. It fails for discrete latents: the map is not differentiable.

keyTerms.definition: log p(x) = log E_q[...] = E_q[log ...] by concavity of log.

recall.question: When would you still marginalize exactly?
recall.answer: Only when K is small and exactness matters.

keyTerms.definition: d/dtheta E_q[f] = E_eps[df/dg·dg/dtheta].
std ~ 1/sqrt(K); 0.05 needs K near 6400.

recall.question: A reparameterized gradient returns exactly 0.0 every step. Root cause and test?
recall.answer: Severed autograd graph (detach on the sampling path). Test: compare against closed form 2·mu and assert nonzero.

keyTerms.definition: q(z) > 0 implies p(x,z) > 0, else the log ratio is infinite.
E_q[log q - log p(z|x)]: where A1's proof starts.

recall.question: Prove the ELBO identity and state the condition.
recall.answer: KL = E_q[log q - log p(z|x)] = E_q[log q - log p(x,z)] + log p(x) = -ELBO + log p(x). Support: q(z) > 0 implies p(x,z) > 0.

keyTerms.definition: Unbiased; variance O(1/K); cost O(K) per step.
K: variance O(1/K), cost O(K) per step.

recall.question: Propose the K=1e6 estimator with properties and cost.
recall.answer: Monte Carlo the expectation: sample z ~ q, average log p(x,z) - log q(z). Unbiased for the ELBO, variance O(1/K), cost O(K) per step, independent of the 1e6 states.

keyTerms.definition: t never moved off init: broken gradient or zero LR on t.
One degree of freedom; contains the true posterior, so it is not the ceiling.

recall.question: Diagnose the -0.62 ELBO ceiling.
recall.answer: The Bernoulli family contains the true posterior, so the ceiling is not the family: the optimizer never moved t off its init. Check: print t over steps.

keyTerms.definition: Large irreducible KL on 50-D correlated posteriors.
Low-rank plus diagonal covariance, O(d·r) params.

recall.question: Cheapest family upgrade for the 50-D correlated posterior?
recall.answer: Low-rank plus diagonal covariance, O(d·r) params, captures the top correlation directions.

keyTerms.definition: One encoder forward pass per point, O(1).
The sacrifice: new points unlike training get worse posteriors.

recall.question: Redesign the 1-point/sec pipeline and state the sacrifice.
recall.answer: Switch to amortized inference: one encoder forward pass per point. Sacrifice: the amortization gap.

keyTerms.definition: A tighter bound is not a better model.
What the settling experiment must hold fixed: inference budgets.

recall.question: Two reasons the higher-ELBO comparison misleads, and the settling experiment?
recall.answer: Reason 1: a higher ELBO can come from a better q with an unchanged or worse p(x). Reason 2: different q families make ELBOs incomparable. Settle: fix one q family, or compare exact/held-out likelihoods with matched inference budgets plus sample-quality checks.
